Safeguard your assets with confidence — even when the engine is off.
Two ways a parked truck loses money overnight.
Rear doors forced at truck stops and unsecured yards. A full trailer can be stripped in minutes.
Tanks siphoned quietly in the dark — a few hundred dollars a hit, repeated across the fleet.
Up to $35 billion a year — and most of it
happens on the truck, not in the warehouse.
Theft of fuel and cargo costs the industry an estimated $17–35 billion annually. Understanding where it happens is the first step to stopping it.
Largest single type — theft from facility
It happens where nobody is watching — overnight, engine off, dashcam asleep.
Clarity or endurance. Until now you had to pick one.
Existing options split into two camps, each with a disqualifying gap. Sentinel is the first camera to sit in the corner nothing else could reach.
Purpose-built for parked assets: the forensic clarity of a camera at the power budget of a sensor. Engine off, still watching — for up to 90 days.
~400 mW while guarding — roughly 1/15 the draw of a traditional camera.
Full-colour, court-ready footage — even at 0.02 lux.
Engine off, on the truck's own battery
Black Light Ultra sees where phones see black
4G · GNSS · Wi-Fi & Bluetooth · onboard storage · I/O with RS-232 — integrated, with a tool-free magnetic mount.
Continuous capture, engine on or off — at a remote yard or a highway rest stop. Every second is recorded, so no event goes unrecorded.
Continuous video capture — engine on or off
Ultra-low-power design sustains months of guarding
High-clarity footage ready for claims and police
Traditional cameras power down when the engine does. Sentinel is the only one still recording when the theft actually happens.
1 frame a second — until someone shows up.

Parked and clear, Sentinel samples the scene one frame per second: a sliver of data that stretches 64 GB across 12 days. The moment a person enters the frame it opens to full-frame video, then drops back when they leave.
Black Light Ultra delivers crisp, full-colour footage in near-total darkness — conditions where smartphones and standard cameras capture nothing at all.
At 0.02 lux, others record darkness. Sentinel records the truth.
Motion alone is noise — animals, headlights, rain, a passer-by. Sentinel reads body posture and behaviour, so it can tell someone walking past your truck from someone working at your fuel tank.
Captures high-clarity video 24/7, in any light
Analyses motion, behaviour and scene context in real time
Detects intent and alerts only when the behaviour warrants it
98.67% alert accuracy — tuned over 7 iterations on 9,447 real field samples
Sentinel is the hub, not just the eyes. It links onboard IoT sensors over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth into one unified alert stream — with video attached to every event.
Axle 2-R at 1.9 bar — rapid leak in transit
Cargo at 80 °C — cold chain at risk
Data tells you what. Video shows you who.
Mounts where it sees the most.
A magnetic, tool-free mount on the cab roof, facing forward — a clean sightline down the flank and the road ahead. No recorder to wire into the cab, and any driver can reposition it.
Forward-facing vantage point covering both flanks
Magnetic mount — minutes, not hours, no drilling
Runs on the truck's own battery, no new wiring
Reposition or redeploy across the fleet in a day
No separate recorder. No wiring maze. Nothing extra to buy — 4G, GNSS, Wi-Fi & Bluetooth, storage and I/O with RS-232 are all in the one unit.
Not a concept. Already earning orders.
Sentinel is still pre-launch — yet 21 customers across five regions are running it on real fleets, and some have already paid for a product that has not shipped.
